key_insight: Time (the flow and speed of events) can be learned as a visual concept from raw video: a model can both recognize when footage is sped up or slowed down and manipulate playback speed by learning temporal transformations from multimodal and structural cues.
problem_solved: Enables automatic perception and control of the passage of time in videos — detecting speed changes, estimating temporal scale, and generating temporally warped (slowed/speeded) video while preserving realism and temporal consistency.
method: Learn a compact "time-flow" representation from unlabeled video by exploiting multimodal signals (e.g., motion, appearance, audio) and natural temporal structure.

Train discriminative heads to classify/regress video speed and generative/time-warping modules to synthesize videos at different speeds, using losses that enforce temporal coherence and perceptual realism.
Use temporal modeling networks and time-warp operators to manipulate frame rates while preserving semantically consistent motion.
impact: Provides AI practitioners with methods to reason about and control temporal scale in video — useful for robust video understanding, data augmentation, temporal editing, simulation, and downstream tasks that require temporal invariance or explicit time manipulation.
visual_elements: Timeline diagram showing original, slowed, and sped-up playback with matched semantic events
Before/after frame strips or short GIFs demonstrating speed-manipulated video synthesis

Bar/line chart comparing performance on speed estimation and realism metrics across baselines
paper_title: Seeing Fast and Slow: Learning the Flow of Time in Videos
paper_authors: Yen-Siang Wu, Rundong Luo, Jingsen Zhu, Tao Tu, Ali Farhadi
